clue.text: Ideas I encountered in part of field doctor brought into line, possibly

indicators.note: the letter I is met inside the word for a part of a field of study, so it sits within it

parts.note: a branch is one part of a field of study or knowledge

indicators.note: the doctor's abbreviation is put inside the rearranged letters of line
possibly says the letters of line may be arranged some other way

explanation.surface: Someone had ideas while out in a field, and a doctor was brought into line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'field' reads as a meadow but means a field of study. 'possibly' scrambles LINE to ILEN before 'brought into' takes the doctor's letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Brainchildren are original ideas or inventions credited to a particular person, so plural ideas fits.

clue.text: Remote working after lawyers showing indication of pressure

indicators.note: after says the anagram comes behind the lawyers in the answer

parts.note: the Bar is the collective body of barristers

indicators.note: working suggests the letters of remote are operated on and put into a new order

explanation.surface: A remote device is working after some lawyers show signs of pressure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Remote' looks like a television handset, but 'working' makes OMETER from its letters. The Bar means barristers collectively.
explanation.definitionFit: A barometer is the instrument whose reading gives atmospheric pressure, so it is an indication of it.

clue.text: Confrontational poem used in commercial

indicators.note: used in says the poem appears in the advert, placed next to its abbreviation

parts.note: an ad is a commercial or advertisement
verse is poetry, a poem

explanation.surface: A confrontational poem has been used in a television commercial.
explanation.definitionFit: Adverse means hostile or opposing, which a confrontational attitude is.

clue.text: Pleasant around even parts of North — observe

indicators.note: around says the word for pleasant wraps the selected letters

parts.note: nice means pleasant

indicators.note: the even-numbered letters, second and fourth, are taken from the word North

explanation.surface: Someone pleasant from around the north is asked to observe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'even parts of' North gives O and T, which NICE goes 'around'.
explanation.definitionFit: To notice is to observe or become aware of something, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Pacific ecosystem rumbled North and cut out

indicators.note: out signals that the letters of the three words are thrown out of order and rearranged

explanation.surface: Some Pacific ecosystem was rumbled, then the north was cut out of it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' shuffles RUMBLED, NORTH and CUT together; 'cut out' looks like one phrase but 'cut' is fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: The Humboldt Current is a cold ocean current off South America supporting a huge marine ecosystem in the Pacific.

clue.text: Official in royal household diverted abnormal child after intervention by old king

indicators.note: the old king's letters intervene, coming between the rearranged letters
diverted means the letters of abnormal child are turned aside into a new order

parts.note: ER is Edward Rex, the title of a former King Edward

explanation.surface: A palace official was diverted by an abnormal child after an old king stepped in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'diverted' scrambles the thirteen letters of the two words, and 'after intervention by' lets the old king break in among them; ER is Edward Rex.
explanation.definitionFit: The Lord Chamberlain is the senior officer of the British royal household, running court business.

clue.text: Study algebraic variables (I'm up in them) prepared for prompt use

parts.note: to read a subject is to study it

indicators.note: the phrase says the turned letters sit inside the two variables

parts.note: x and y are the usual letters for unknowns in algebra

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the letters of I'm are read bottom to top

explanation.surface: A student studying algebra, deep in variables, is ready to use them at short notice.
explanation.walkthrough: The bracket reads as an aside about being absorbed in the maths; 'up' is a reversal because this is a down entry, and 'in them' points back to the variables.
explanation.definitionFit: Ready-mix describes concrete or food mixed in advance, made available for immediate use.

clue.text: We will block number given places at table? It's easily done

indicators.note: to block something is to sit in its way, so we goes in the middle of the other letters

parts.note: people given places at a table sat there

explanation.surface: Guests ask whether they will block a numbered seat when given their places at a dinner table.
explanation.walkthrough: 'will block' is the insertion signal. 'given places at table' describes diners who sat down, so it supplies a past tense verb rather than seats.
explanation.definitionFit: No sweat is an informal idiom meaning no trouble at all, a task done with ease.

clue.text: Looks to dispose of stone god

indicators.note: the clue says the stone abbreviation is got rid of from the looking word

parts.note: stares means looks fixedly
ST is the abbreviation for stone, the British unit of weight

explanation.surface: Someone's looks are enough to make them dispose of a stone god.
explanation.walkthrough: A stone is a British weight of fourteen pounds, abbreviated ST.
explanation.definitionFit: Ares is the Greek deity of war, matching the bare definition god.

clue.text: Fix support for pot after front falls off

indicators.note: the first letter is lost from the support word, its front dropping away

parts.note: a trivet is a small stand on which a hot pot rests

explanation.surface: Someone must fix the stand for a pot after its front has fallen off.
explanation.definitionFit: To rivet is to fasten or fix firmly, as with metal pins.

clue.text: Duck answer when probing business deal?

indicators.note: a probe goes inside, so the answer abbreviation is put within the deal word

parts.note: a merger is a deal combining two companies

explanation.surface: A question about ducking an answer when someone probes a business deal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Duck' looks like a verb, dodging an answer, but it is the bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A merganser is a fish-eating diving bird with a serrated bill, a kind of duck.

clue.text: Way of working: very ornate, disregarding one old leather

parts.note: MO is modus operandi, a way of working

indicators.note: one of the repeated round letters in the ornate word is ignored and dropped

parts.note: rococo describes highly elaborate decoration

explanation.surface: A craftsman's way of working was very ornate but disregarded one piece of old leather.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disregarding one' drops one of the three Os from ROCOCO, leaving ROCCO.
explanation.definitionFit: Morocco is a fine goatskin leather traditionally used for bookbinding, long established.

clue.text: Yen to tuck into ice-creams — source of some reticence

indicators.note: tuck into sounds like eating, but here the yen letter is tucked inside the cones

parts.note: cones are ice-creams served in wafer cones
Y is the abbreviation for yen, the Japanese currency

indicators.note: the source of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A yen to tuck into ice-creams prompts some shyness in the eater.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to tuck into' looks like eating; it puts Y inside CONES.
explanation.definitionFit: Coyness is shy or reserved behaviour, so it is a kind of reticence.

clue.text: Satisfied about husband backsliding? Not us

indicators.note: sliding back means the letters are read in the reverse direction
about says the satisfied word wraps round the husband letter

parts.note: met as in demands met, satisfied

explanation.surface: A wife, satisfied, talks about her husband backsliding; not her fault, she says.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts H in MET for MEHT, and 'backsliding' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: The pronoun for other people, the opposite group from ourselves, is what not us means.

clue.text: One of French, most celebrated in Cannes, primarily as visionary

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
de is the French word for of
the A-list is the most celebrated group of stars

indicators.note: primarily means the first letters of the following words are taken

explanation.surface: One of the French stars, most celebrated at the Cannes film festival, is seen as a visionary.
explanation.definitionFit: Idealistic people pursue lofty, perhaps impractical aims, as a dreamer or visionary does.

clue.text: International player being dealt with submissively

parts.note: a cap is a player chosen to represent their country
in hand means being dealt with or under control

explanation.surface: An international footballer is dealt with in a submissive manner.
explanation.walkthrough: In British sport a player chosen for the national team wins a cap, so a cap is an international.
explanation.definitionFit: Cap in hand is an idiom for approaching someone humbly, asking a favour.

clue.text: Use of cosmetic items getting family in panic

indicators.note: in says the family word is placed inside the panic word

parts.note: a scare is a sudden fright or panic
kin means family or relatives

explanation.surface: Using cosmetics causes a family panic.
explanation.definitionFit: Skincare is the routine of applying creams and lotions to keep skin healthy.

clue.text: Bucks laid out, investing in gems mostly, or toy design

indicators.note: to invest is to put something into a holding, so the anagram goes inside the gems
mostly means the word for gems loses its last letter

parts.note: rubies are red gemstones

indicators.note: laid out means the letters of bucks are spread out in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone's bucks are laid out, investing in gems mostly, or in a toy design.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bucks' reads as dollars spent, but 'laid out' scrambles its letters into KSCUB; 'investing in' then wraps the trimmed gems around them.
explanation.definitionFit: The Rubik's Cube is a famous puzzle toy, a design by Ernő Rubik with rotating coloured faces.

clue.text: Very hot fuel filling container? Good

indicators.note: the fuel word fills the container, sitting inside it

parts.note: a bin is a container
oil is a fuel

explanation.surface: Is very hot fuel filling a container a good idea?
explanation.definitionFit: Boiling is used informally for extremely high temperatures, as in a scorching day.

clue.text: Misinterpret return of crude power

indicators.note: return means the letters of the crude word come back the other way

parts.note: raw means crude or unrefined
P is the symbol for power in physics

explanation.surface: Someone misreads the return of crude oil's power.
explanation.definitionFit: To warp facts is to twist or distort them, giving a false interpretation.

clue.text: A fabulous figure — a centrist politician and a graduate …

parts.note: LIB is short for Liberal, a party of the centre
BA is a Bachelor of Arts, a graduate

explanation.surface: A legendary figure turns out to be a centrist politician who also has a degree.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links into the next clue, but this clue stands alone.
explanation.definitionFit: Ali Baba is the woodcutter hero of a tale from the Arabian Nights, a character of fable.

clue.text: … affected American college centre

parts.note: camp means theatrically affected or mannered
US stands for the United States, so American

explanation.surface: An affected American shows up at a college centre.
explanation.definitionFit: A campus is the grounds and buildings at the heart of a university or college.

clue.text: The champion, dismissing bridge team as less substantial

indicators.note: dismissing means the bridge pair's letters are sent away from the combined words

parts.note: a champion is the winner
in bridge, East and West form one partnership, abbreviated EW

explanation.surface: The champion dismisses a bridge team for being too weak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dismissing' removes E and W from THEWINNER; bridge is played by two pairs, North-South and East-West.
explanation.definitionFit: Thinner means more slender or flimsy, so having less substance.

clue.text: Extract of dirty poem, one showing errant character

indicators.note: Extract of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: An extract from a dirty poem shows the poet's wayward character.
explanation.walkthrough: 'errant character' suggests a wayward person, but the character is a printed letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A printing mistake displays a wrong letter, a character gone astray on the page.

clue.text: Material that's grand in fashionable shift

parts.note: material and real both mean actual, substantial

indicators.note: in says the grand letter goes inside the word for fashionable

parts.note: in means fashionable, as in the in thing
G is short for grand, a thousand

explanation.surface: Material that's grand in a fashionable shift dress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Material' and 'shift' suggest fabric and a dress, but they are the adjective and the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To realign is to change position or alignment, a shift of arrangement.

clue.text: Formal state banquet's second prepared with spring vegetables

parts.note: prim means stiffly formal or proper
to aver is to state firmly

indicators.note: second picks the letter in position two of the banquet word

explanation.surface: The second course at a formal state banquet is prepared with spring vegetables.
explanation.definitionFit: Primavera, Italian for springtime, describes pasta dishes made with fresh spring produce.

clue.text: Extreme characters engaged in a lot of sport in open space

indicators.note: the extreme characters are engaged within the shortened sport word
a lot of means most but not all of the sport word, losing its last letter

parts.note: to play is to engage in sport
A and Z are the letters at the two extremes of the alphabet

explanation.surface: Extreme characters engaged in a lot of sport in a public open space.
explanation.definitionFit: A plaza is a public square or open area in a town, from Spanish.

clue.text: Morag's crying a lot about Queen's congratulatory message?

parts.note: greeting is Scots for weeping, and Morag is a Scottish name

indicators.note: about says the word for a lot goes round the queen letter

parts.note: scads means a lot, a scad being a large amount
R is from Regina, Latin for queen

explanation.surface: Morag is crying a lot about the Queen's congratulatory message.
explanation.walkthrough: In Scottish English to greet is to weep, so the Scottish name signals the dialect word.
explanation.definitionFit: A greetings card carries good wishes, often to congratulate someone, hence the question mark for an example.
